cues.text: A model learns by sliding downhill — along the steepest way down.
Its position is a set of weights. The slope it feels is the gradient.
Each layer sums weighted inputs, then bends the result with a nonlinearity.
Stack enough of them and the network can approximate any continuous function.
A neuron multiplies each input by its weight, then adds them up.
Add a bias, and the result z becomes the input to an activation.
The sigmoid squeezes any number into a probability between zero and one.
Training minimises an average loss over the data.
Each step moves the weights against the gradient, scaled by a learning rate.
Repeat those two moves and the whole function is learned.
